newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners still shunning costly foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners still shunning costly foreign crudes.

text.p: Most U.S. refiners continued to shun foreign crudes Tuesday in favor of alternative domestic grades as a result of the narrow trans-Atlantic arbitrage.
One Gulf Coast refiner, however, was heard to have picked up a delivered Brent cargo in a confidential deal, and traders said more Brent cargoes could be making their way into the U.S. soon.

"The arb is still closed, but with LLS (Light Louisiana Sweet) at $1 differential, you could make something work," one trader said, citing a notional delivered price of Jan West Texas Intermediate plus 40 cents a barrel.
The January WTI/Brent spread widened slightly to 75-80 cents and held steady at 90-95 cents for the corresponding February months compared to Monday.
In Latin American trade, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol tendered 400,000 barrels of South Blend at an unconfirmed price of around Dec WTI minus $2.35 a barrel.
At that price, traders speculated that the cargo went to a Central or South American destination.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a number of partial cargoes of Jan Brent changed hands at $23.30-35 a barrel, a few cents down from the IPE settlement.
Intermonth spreads strengthened, with Brent Dec/Jan at 27-30 cents, up from 21-25 cents in the late London session.
